package_info.package_versions: All published versions during the campaign
package_info.why_malicious: These packages were intentionally created in bulk as spam or with malicious intent. They contain metadata fields (such as description, homepage, or README) with links to scam, malware, or referral sites. The mass publication of these packages caused a denial of service on the npm registry, disrupted legitimate package discovery, and exposed users to further attacks via SEO poisoning, malicious redirection, and potential malware infection.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or when viewing package metadata, the package exposes links to external malicious or scam websites via metadata fields, leading users to visit these domains and increasing the risk of exploitation or redirection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate packages do not use metadata fields to promote unrelated or known malicious domains. The presence of links to scam, malware, or referral sites in package.json or README.md is a strong indicator of malicious intent, as it attempts to lure users to external threats.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages use metadata fields for project-related information, such as documentation or official homepages, not for advertising or redirecting to unrelated, scam, or malicious sites.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may link to their own documentation or project homepage, but never to unrelated, suspicious, or known malicious domains.
key_indicators: Metadata fields (description, homepage, README) containing links to unrelated or known malicious domains
Descriptions or documentation with referral, scam, or malware links
Absence of legitimate project content in metadata

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the code initiates a network request to a malicious website by opening or fetching an external URL, which may redirect the user, exfiltrate data, or facilitate further compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Code that automatically performs network requests to external, suspicious domains during installation is highly suspicious, especially when the domains are associated with scams or malware. This behavior can be used for user redirection, data exfiltration, or to trigger additional malicious payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not perform unsolicited network requests to unrelated or malicious domains during installation. Any network activity should be limited to legitimate update checks or dependency downloads from trusted sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may fetch dependencies or check for updates from their own servers, but not from unrelated, suspicious, or known malicious domains.
key_indicators: Network requests to suspicious or known malicious domains during installation
Automatic redirection or data exfiltration at install-time
Presence of code in entry files that opens or fetches external URLs unrelated to the package's functionality

attack_chain.action: Threat actor publishes a large number of empty or spam packages with metadata fields containing links to malicious or scam websites.
attack_chain.leads_to: Users or automated systems encounter these packages via search, dependency resolution, or browsing the npm registry.

attack_chain.action: Users viewing package metadata or documentation are lured to visit malicious or scam websites through embedded links.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential malware infection, referral scam, credential harvesting, or further exploitation via external sites.

attack_chain.action: Some packages execute code at install-time to open or fetch malicious websites, initiating unsolicited network requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Possible data exfiltration, user redirection, or further compromise of the user's environment.

attack_chain.action: Mass publication of these packages causes a denial of service on the npm registry, overwhelming legitimate package discovery and registry operations.
attack_chain.leads_to: Service disruption for legitimate users and increased risk of exposure to malicious packages.

behavioral_signatures: Packages with metadata fields (description, homepage, README) containing links to unrelated, suspicious, or known malicious domains
Packages that perform unsolicited network requests to suspicious or malicious domains at install-time
Mass publication of empty or near-empty packages with similar metadata patterns in a short time frame
file_indicators: package.json with homepage or description fields pointing to suspicious or known malicious domains
README.md files containing scam, referral, or malware links
index.js or main entry files with code that opens or fetches external URLs unrelated to the package's stated purpose
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains associated with scams, malware, or referral campaigns during package installation
Unusual spikes in requests to npm registry endpoints from new or low-reputation packages
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages whose metadata fields (description, homepage, README) contain links to known malicious, unrelated, or suspicious domains. Flag packages that perform unsolicited network requests to suspicious domains during installation. Detect mass publication of empty or near-empty packages with similar metadata patterns, and correlate with known scam or malware campaigns. Use threat intelligence to maintain an up-to-date list of malicious domains and referral links. Implement automated scanning of package metadata and install-time behaviors to identify and block malicious packages before exposure.
